title: Employee Onboarding Agent
problem: New employee onboarding spans 6–10 systems — HRIS, Active Directory, benefits portal, document signing, calendar, and access control. HR teams manually coordinate each step, leading to delayed access provisioning (avg 3–5 days), missed benefits enrollments, and compliance gaps from incomplete documentation. Each error costs hours of back-and-forth between HR, IT, and Legal.
solution: An orchestrator agent triggers on a signed offer letter event and fans out to four specialist subagents running in parallel: IdentityAgent (provisions Entra ID account + M365 licenses), BenefitsAgent (enrolls in health, 401k, stock plans), DocumentAgent (routes NDA and I-9 via DocuSign, archives signed copies), and CalendarAgent (schedules onboarding week using Microsoft Graph). Any compensation or equity adjustment requires explicit manager approval through a HITL gate before the IdentityAgent proceeds. Full onboarding state is persisted in a durable workflow — a mid-run failure retries from the last checkpoint, never duplicates a provisioning action.
whoItsFor: HR Operations Teams, IT Provisioning, People Ops at mid-to-large enterprises
workflowSteps: Trigger: signed offer letter event fires from HRIS (Workday/SAP SuccessFactors) or e-signature webhook
OrchestratorAgent reads employee record — extracts role, department, location, start date, compensation tier
If compensation tier requires equity grant: HITL approval gate — manager approves or modifies before parallel fan-out
Parallel fan-out to 4 specialist subagents (async, decoupled via message queue):
IdentityAgent: provisions Entra ID account, assigns M365 licenses, sets department group memberships
BenefitsAgent: enrolls employee in health plan, 401k, ESPP based on eligibility rules
DocumentAgent: sends NDA + I-9 via DocuSign, monitors completion, archives signed PDFs to SharePoint
CalendarAgent: schedules orientation day, manager 1:1, IT setup session via Microsoft Graph
OrchestratorAgent polls specialist status from Cosmos DB state store
On all-complete: sends welcome email with access credentials, benefits summary, and calendar links
On any failure: retries from last checkpoint (idempotency keys prevent duplicate provisioning); after 3 retries, escalates to HR ops queue
keyInsights: The HITL gate placement is critical — it must fire before any provisioning begins, not after. Placing it mid-workflow creates a partial-state problem where the employee has an AD account but no approved equity grant. The durable workflow pattern (Temporal/Azure Durable Functions) prevents the worst failure mode: a crash after AD provisioning but before benefits enrollment leaves the employee partially onboarded with no automated recovery. Idempotency keys on each provisioning action ensure retries are safe.

architectureNotes: Deploy as a coordinator-specialist multi-agent system. The OrchestratorAgent (Azure AI Agent Service or LangGraph) reads the triggering employee record and fans out to specialist agents via Azure Service Bus topics — one topic per specialist, allowing each to consume and process independently. Cosmos DB acts as the saga state store: each specialist writes its completion status on success; the orchestrator polls and gates the final welcome-email step on all-complete status. The HITL approval gate uses a durable task pause (Temporal signal or Azure Durable Functions external event) so the workflow waits indefinitely without holding a thread. DocuSign webhook triggers the DocumentAgent on signature completion — the agent does not poll. All provisioning tools carry idempotency keys derived from the employee ID + action type, ensuring safe retries after partial failures.

tools: Microsoft Graph API (M365 license assignment, group membership)
Azure Cosmos DB (saga state + audit log)

failureModes.mode: AD provisioning succeeds but benefits enrollment fails
failureModes.mitigation: Saga state in Cosmos DB tracks each specialist status independently. On benefits failure, orchestrator retries BenefitsAgent with idempotency key — AD account is not re-provisioned.
DocumentAgent polls DocuSign status API as fallback with exponential backoff. Signed documents are archived only after confirmed webhook or poll confirmation.

failureModes.mode: HITL gate timeout — manager does not respond
failureModes.mitigation: Durable workflow sends reminder at 24h and 48h. After 72h, escalates to HR ops queue with a pre-filled approval form. Onboarding is blocked until explicit approval — no auto-approval fallback for equity grants.

failureModes.mode: Employee record missing required fields (e.g. benefits eligibility tier)
failureModes.mitigation: OrchestratorAgent validates the employee record schema before fan-out. Missing required fields trigger an immediate escalation to HR ops with a structured error report — no partial provisioning begins.

scalingConsiderations: At 100+ hires/month: use batch fan-out with Service Bus queues to prevent Entra ID provisioning rate limit (50 accounts/min). Distribute over time windows.
Multi-region: pin each employee's saga state to their hiring region's Cosmos DB partition to meet data residency requirements.
Union or regulatory environments: inject a configurable approval-rules engine (not hardcoded equity threshold) so HR can adjust approval triggers without code changes.

integrations.notes: Webhook on offer-accepted event; employee record fetch via Workday REST API
Provision user account, assign licenses, set group memberships via Graph API
Send envelope via eSignature API; receive completion event via webhook
REST API enrollment for health, 401k, ESPP — idempotency key per plan per employee
Create calendar events for orientation, 1:1, IT setup via Microsoft Graph
